title: gsang ba snying thig gi kha byang nyi snying nang gsal ba ltar
shelf_note: Drametse (Bhutan) Nyingma manuscript bundle, EAP via BL: a commentary on a tantra 'worn for liberation' (btags grol), a thod rgal practice manual (vajra chains, gazes, signs), a rdzogs chen anatomy of mind and wisdom, and an empowerment rite. This is the Snying thig material the title names.
structure_note: Each image is a board of four loose leaves (I5). On p.33 and p.89 the leaf texts do not run on from one leaf to the next (p.33 leaf 3 ends 'ལུས་ཀྱི་བྱ་བ་དང་', leaf 4 opens 'གསེར་གྱི་སྙིང་པོ'), so one site 'page' is four separate openings, not a reading order. The text carries <leaf-break/> and the English marks each seam with an ellipsis, so the translator invents no bridges. The bundle holds several distinct works: p.33 uses the ༔ gter-tsheg hand; p.89/135/203 are in a shad-punctuated hand with red rubrics. On p.203 the third leaf is a title leaf, which suggests a new text begins inside this record. Counts disagree: the book field says pages_ocr 95, while structure counts 246 pages with OCR; 89 of 246 are translated. One printed-number repeat, from 5 readable numbers: too few to judge.

book_verdict: Leaf-by-leaf, the transcription matches the board photographs line for line, and the English is careful and close. But every page is a board of four non-consecutive leaves, and the bundle holds several works under one title, one of whose title leaves was skipped.
reader_summary: This is a bundle of Snying thig manuscripts from Drametse: a btags-grol commentary, a thod rgal manual and an empowerment rite. The Tibetan on each leaf is the leaf's own text, and the English follows it closely, with seams marked. A reader must know that one 'page' here is four separate leaves photographed together, not a continuous passage.

title: las 'brel rtsal gyi gter ma rta mgrin gnyen po lha gsum
shelf_note: A gter ma cycle of Hayagriva, Vajrapani and Garuda (the 'three deities'), for subduing nagas: empowerments, naga-illness diagnostics, vase treasures, and a mantra appendix spoken as Padmasambhava. Drametse manuscript.
structure_note: Each image is a board of three loose leaves (I5). On p.18, leaf 1 ends mid-formula 'ཁྱོད་ཀྱིས་དབང་མཆོག་' and leaf 2 opens 'བྲན་དང་ཁོལ་པོ', so the leaves on one image are not consecutive. The text carries <leaf-break/> and the English leaves the seams open. printed_backsteps 4 out of 8 readable printed numbers: the margin numerals are small cursive leaf numbers, so these are probably misreads, not a scrambled scan. Counts disagree: the book field says pages_ocr 86, while structure counts 172 pages with OCR; 73 of 172 are translated.

book_verdict: Leaf by leaf, the transcription is right and the English is a usable, close rendering of a naga-subjugation cycle. A few glosses are guessed and stated as fact, and the three-leaf boards break the reading order.
reader_summary: This is a Hayagriva–Vajrapani–Garuda gter ma for taming nagas: empowerments, signs of naga illness, and treasure-vase rites. The Tibetan is the leaves' own text. The English is trustworthy for the ritual sequence, but not for the occasional glossed term, such as 'King of the Impossible'. Each page shows three separate leaves, not a continuous passage.

title: sbyin sreg gi skor
shelf_note: A fierce (drag po) fire-offering manual from a gter gzhung: hearth measurements, the twelve substances with their mantras, a praise of the fire god, then Vajrakilaya 'liberation' (bsgral) of an effigy. Drametse manuscript booklet.
structure_note: A sewn booklet: each image shows two pages, top and bottom, and the text runs on from top to bottom (p.7: 'འབུལ་བ་དང' → 'མེ་ཉིད་ཡེ་ཤེས་ཀྱི་མེར'), so reading order holds. 38 pages: 25 have OCR, 13 are translated (the book field says pages_ocr 18), so most of the booklet is unread in English.

book_verdict: The transcription is clean and in order in a readable booklet hand. The English is good on the ritual inventory and liturgy, but p.20 swaps left for right in the Kilaya visualisation and leaves a broken note tag. Only about a third of the booklet is translated.
reader_summary: This is a fierce homa manual (hearth, twelve substances, mantras, fire-god praise) followed by a Vajrakilaya effigy-liberation rite. The Tibetan is the page's own text. The English can be trusted for the sequence of the rite, but should be checked against the Tibetan for iconographic detail.

title: sde brgyad gser skyems (EAP105-1-3-195)
shelf_note: A golden libation (gser skyems) to the eight classes, with a Padma Heruka self-visualisation, a long dedication to the local and regional deities, and a torma offering to the nagas. Short Drametse manuscript booklet.
structure_note: A small booklet: two pages per image, top and bottom, and the text runs on from top to bottom (p.10: '…སྒྲུབ' → 'པའི་གྲོགས་མཛོད་ཅིག'). 22 pages; all have OCR but only 9 are translated (the book field says pages_ocr 10). printed_backsteps 2 from only 3 readable numbers: probably misreads of the tiny leaf numerals.

tr_errors.problem: sdig (threatening mudra) rendered as 'scorpion'

tr_errors.problem: rgyal btsun (gyalpo and btsun mo spirits) taken literally as 'kings and nuns'

ocr_errors.problem: minor misreading; the English is right

tr_errors.problem: a spelling read as a proper place name, without flagging it

book_verdict: A short, sound record: the transcription matches the booklet pages, reading order holds, and the English is a faithful rendering of a standard gser skyems liturgy with only a few small slips.
reader_summary: This is a golden libation to the eight classes of spirits and the local deities, as practised at Drametse. The Tibetan is the page's own text. The English can be trusted as a working translation, apart from an odd gloss such as 'scorpion gesture' for the threatening mudra.
